rows.verified: The asbestos dutyholder may be a building owner, landlord or organisation clearly responsible for maintenance or repair.
The dutyholder must protect people who work in or otherwise use the building from asbestos exposure risks.
The duty to manage covers non-domestic premises and common parts of multi-occupancy domestic premises.
Dutyholders must assess whether asbestos-containing materials are present, including their amount, location and condition.
Materials must be presumed to contain asbestos unless there is strong evidence that they do not.
An up-to-date record or register of the location and condition of asbestos-containing or presumed materials is required.
The dutyholder must assess the risk of exposure to airborne fibres and put an asbestos management plan into action.
The asbestos management plan must be monitored and reviewed every 12 months or sooner when necessary.
Asbestos controls depend on building age, material type, location, condition, accessibility, planned disturbance, occupancy and survey quality.
Asbestos evidence is building-, material-, condition- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level exposure or disease probability.
Employers and people in control of premises must identify, assess, manage, prevent or control legionella risks and keep appropriate records.
Water systems can support legionella growth when water temperatures are between 20°C and 45°C.
A foreseeable legionella risk can arise where a system creates or spreads breathable water droplets.
Stored or recirculated water and nutrients such as rust, sludge, scale or biofilm can support legionella growth.
Common sources include cooling towers, evaporative condensers, hot and cold water systems and spa pools.
A competent responsible person with sufficient authority, skills, knowledge and system experience must be appointed to manage identified risks.
Using a water-treatment contractor does not remove the competent person's responsibility to ensure work meets the required standard.
Sites with cooling towers or evaporative condensers may have to notify the local authority in writing and update it when equipment is no longer used.
Legionella controls depend on water-system design, temperature, stagnation, aerosol generation, maintenance, occupancy and monitoring results.
Legionella evidence is system-, operation-, time- and population-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
